    "summary": "At 32x256 (8192 FP32 elements) the arithmetic is negligible; the measured 14.336us baseline / 10.24us candidate-03 is almost entirely per-op launch and Python dispatch cost (baseline 5 launches incl. a redundant clone, candidate-03 4 launches). The only remaining structural lever in eager PyTorch is the number of launches per call, because relu(x*1.25 + y*0.75 - 0.125) cannot be expressed in fewer than 4 builtin elementwise ops (addcmul/lerp/add-with-alpha formulations all still need a scale, a shift and a clamp). Recording the chain into a CUDA graph collapses those 4 launches into one. Note the declared target (99.9999% p50 improvement => ~1.4e-11 s) is physically unreachable for any GPU implementation; the honest objective is minimizing per-call launch overhead.",
    "bottlenecks": [
      "per-op CUDA launch overhead x4 per run() call",
      "Python-level dispatcher/arg-parsing cost per torch op call",
      "no operator fusion available in eager mode for this 3-term affine + clamp expression"
    ]
  },
  "candidates": [
    {
      "id": "candidate-04",
      "title": "CUDA-graph replay of the affine+relu chain (1 launch instead of 4) with clone-on-return and eager fallback",
      "hypothesis": "The p50 metric is launch-bound, so collapsing the four elementwise kernels into one replayed graph removes ~3 of 4 launches and most of the per-call Python dispatch, cutting p50 well below candidate-03's 10.24us while producing bit-identical numerics (same kernels, same order).",
      "change": "run.py: run(inputs) now looks up a cache keyed by (x.data_ptr, y.data_ptr, device indices, shapes, strides). Cache miss (first call per signature, budget 16) => warm up 3x on a side stream, capture the unchanged _affine_relu chain with torch.cuda.graph, replay once and store (graph, static_out). Cache hit => graph.replay() then return static_out.clone(). Any capture exception permanently disables capture (global flag + cache clear) and every subsequent call uses the plain eager _affine_relu chain. Non-CUDA or non-FP32 inputs go straight to eager. Inputs are only read (never mutated) and the caller never receives an aliased buffer.",
      "files": ["run.py"],
      "sourceReferences": [
        "baseline run.py (naive_v0, 14.336000196635723us, local-shared-gpu)",
        "MIS_MU1ZMD3E round-3 candidate-03 measurement 10.239999741315842us, correctness 4/4 pass both profiles"

        "If the harness allocates fresh input tensors with fresh (never-recycled) addresses on every repeat, the 16-graph budget is consumed during warmup and measurement falls back to the eager path (no regression vs candidate-03, no gain).",
        "CUDA graph capture may be unavailable or refused in the shared-GPU runner (driver/context/pool restrictions); handled by a try/except that disables capture permanently and falls back to the correctness-verified eager chain.",
        "First call per input signature pays capture cost (~ms) inside warmup; measured repeats should be pure replays, but if warmup were shorter than the number of signatures a single slow repeat could inflate p95/max.",
        "The graph reads live input buffers, so semantics depend only on shape/stride/dtype/device matching the captured signature; a keyed mismatch (including stride/dtype/device) forces a new capture or the eager path."
      ]
    }
  ],
  "recommendedCandidate": "candidate-04",

    "type": "candidate.plan",
    "title": "Run candidate-04 through the serialized GPU queue (correctness then full benchmark)",

candidateEvaluations.title: CUDA-graph replay of the affine+relu chain (1 launch instead of 4) with clone-on-return and eager fallback
candidateEvaluations.hypothesis: The p50 metric is launch-bound, so collapsing the four elementwise kernels into one replayed graph removes ~3 of 4 launches and most of the per-call Python dispatch, cutting p50 well below candidate-03's 10.24us while producing bit-identical numerics (same kernels, same order).
candidateEvaluations.change: run.py: run(inputs) now looks up a cache keyed by (x.data_ptr, y.data_ptr, device indices, shapes, strides). Cache miss (first call per signature, budget 16) => warm up 3x on a side stream, capture the unchanged _affine_relu chain with torch.cuda.graph, replay once and store (graph, static_out). Cache hit => graph.replay() then return static_out.clone(). Any capture exception permanently disables capture (global flag + cache clear) and every subsequent call uses the plain eager _affine_relu chain. Non-CUDA or non-FP32 inputs go straight to eager. Inputs are only read (never mutated) and the caller never receives an aliased buffer.
